name: Potassiummaxxing

lead: Potassiummaxxing is a diet and lifestyle approach of eating potassium-rich foods, with bananas and coconut water as the common examples, to support fluid balance and muscle function.
Proponents link balanced sodium and potassium to a less bloated look and to better training; potassium works with sodium to keep fluid balance and enable muscle contraction.

paras: People add foods such as bananas, coconut water, potatoes, avocados and beans to their regular diet.

Hyperkalemia, excess blood potassium, is the most serious adverse effect and is most common in people with kidney failure; it can cause weakness and abnormal heart rhythm. Supplements most often cause stomach upset.

chain: Less puffy look and normal muscle contraction
angle.text: Followers raise potassium through food to support fluid balance and muscle function. The aim is a leaner, less bloated appearance.

lead: Potassiummaxxing is the practice of deliberately increasing dietary potassium, typically through foods such as bananas and coconut water, in looksmaxxing and fitness circles.

Potassium is the main intracellular ion and helps maintain fluid and electrolyte balance; with sodium it creates the membrane potential behind nerve signalling and muscle contraction [1]. Followers link this to a less puffy appearance and better muscle function.
Coconut water contains about 250 mg of potassium per 100 g [2]. US adequate intakes are 3,400 mg a day for men and 2,600 mg for women [1].

paras: High-potassium foods include kiwifruit, orange juice, potatoes, coconut, avocados and beans [1]. Coconut water carries about 250 mg per 100 g [2].
Hyperkalemia is most common with renal failure and can cause tingling, muscle weakness and arrhythmia [1]. Coconut water marketing claims have been the subject of class-action suits [2].
